title: Maximum Font to Fit a Sentence in a Screen
statement:
The string `text` has to be shown on a single line of a screen that is `w` pixels wide and `h` pixels tall. You may pick one font size from `fonts`, which lists the available sizes in strictly increasing order. Character sizes are not given directly; instead you receive a `fontInfo` object whose two methods each run in O(1):

- `fontInfo.getWidth(fontSize, ch)` returns how wide the single character `ch` is at size `fontSize`.
- `fontInfo.getHeight(fontSize)` returns how tall every character is at size `fontSize`.

At a given size, the text is as wide as the sum of `getWidth(fontSize, text[i])` over all indexes `i`, and as tall as `getHeight(fontSize)`. It fits when that width is at most `w` and that height is at most `h`. Both methods return the same value whenever they are called with the same arguments, and neither shrinks as the size grows: `getHeight(fontSize) <= getHeight(fontSize + 1)` and `getWidth(fontSize, ch) <= getWidth(fontSize + 1, ch)` for every letter `ch`.

Return the largest size in `fonts` at which `text` fits, or `-1` when it fits at none of them.

Your function is `maxFont(text, w, h, fonts, fontInfo)`. Each case is written as `[text, w, h, fonts]`, and the judge builds `fontInfo` from one fixed font: `getHeight(fontSize)` is `fontSize`, and `getWidth(fontSize, ch)` is `fontSize + p % 3`, where `p` is the position of `ch` in the alphabet (`a` = 1, `b` = 2, ..., `z` = 26). Solve it through `fontInfo` only, as if the formula were unknown.
constraints: text contains only lowercase English letters
fonts is sorted in increasing order and has no duplicates
getWidth and getHeight each take O(1) time
signature: int maxFont(String text, int w, int h, int[] fonts)
api: maxFont(text: string, w: number, h: number, fonts: number[], fontInfo: { getWidth(fontSize: number, ch: string): number; getHeight(fontSize: number): number }): number
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every size in `fonts` and adding up the text's width each time costs O(|fonts| · |text|). The guarantee that widths and heights never shrink as the size grows makes "does the text fit?" monotone along the sorted `fonts`: every size up to some point fits and every larger one does not. So the answer is the last `true` in a run of `true`s followed by `false`s, which binary search finds with only O(log |fonts|) fit checks.

## Approach

1. Write `fits(fontSize)`: reject at once if `getHeight` exceeds `h`; otherwise add up `getWidth` for every character, stopping as soon as `width` passes `w`.
2. Binary search the indexes of `fonts` with `left` and `right`, keeping `answer = -1`.
3. If `fonts[mid]` fits, record it in `answer` and look for a bigger size with `left = mid + 1`.
4. Otherwise every size from `mid` upward is too big, so set `right = mid - 1`.
5. When the range is empty, `answer` is the largest fitting size, or `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`text = "helloworld"`, `w = 80`, `h = 20`, `fonts = [6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 36]`.

- `mid = 4`, size 14: tall enough, but the running width passes 80 at the sixth letter, `w` (16 + 16 + 14 + 14 + 14 + 16 = 90), so `right = 3`.
- `mid = 1`, size 8: the full width is 87 > 80, so `right = 0`.
- `mid = 0`, size 6: height 6 and width 67 both fit, so `answer = 6` and `left = 1`.

The range is empty, and the result is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(|text| · log |fonts|): each of the O(log |fonts|) checks reads every character at most once.
- Space: O(1) besides the input.

## Pitfalls

- Every character has its own width: `text.length * getWidth(size, text[0])` is wrong.
- Check both limits; a size can be narrow enough yet too tall.
- Return the font size `fonts[mid]`, not the index `mid`, and `-1` when even `fonts[0]` fails.
- With `text.length` up to 50,000 and sizes up to 10^5, the width can reach about 5 · 10^9; stop summing once it passes `w`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `fits(fontSize)` | whether `text` fits on the screen at that size |
| `width` | running width of the text at the size being checked |
| `left`, `right` | the range of `fonts` indexes still undecided |
| `mid` | the index tested in this round |
| `answer` | the largest size known to fit, or `-1` |

narration.2: A helper decides whether the whole text fits at one font size.
narration.3: If even the height is too big, this size cannot work.
narration.6: Start adding up the widths of the characters at this size.
narration.8: Add the width of the next character.
narration.9: Once the running width passes w, there is no need to read further.
narration.13: Every character fit within w and the height fit within h.
narration.16: The search covers indexes of fonts, from the first...
narration.18: No size is known to fit yet, so the default is -1.
narration.19: Keep searching while some index is still undecided.
narration.20: Test the size in the middle of the undecided range.
narration.21: Fit is monotone: if this size fits, every smaller size fits too.
narration.22: Remember it as the best size so far.
narration.23: Look only at bigger sizes from now on.
narration.25: It does not fit, so no bigger size fits either; look at smaller ones.
narration.28: The search has ended on the largest size that fits, or -1 if none does.
